notes.text:
Deliverables are independent-review.md, whole-proof.md, whole-source-application-ledger.md, whole-proof-coverage.md, original-scope-and-noncircularity.md, acceptance-decision.json and native-notes.json. The latter contains the full reconstructed seven-note proof chain. Supporting artifacts include source-qualification-addendum.md, bounded-evidence-input.json, retained inputs and reports. Rerun commands are python audit_packets.py; python own_evidence.py; python finish_review.py. These fresh programs audit data and finite observations; they do not execute supplied programs or compile TeX.

The sole incoming mathematical support is the ENTIRE qualified G331, including its complete primary-model cone paper, mandatory annotation, ledger and scope. Current, historical controller and historical worker grant objects agree. Its four separate component bodies agree with their embedded grant bodies after stripping marker-boundary whitespace. G331 supplies no products, independent Cartier intersections, intersection continuity, locality, envelopes, energy or arbitrary-model cofinality.

For excellent reduced local R of dimension n>0 and proper primary gauge a, the domain is all centred semivaluations X_a, including nonminimal supports. C is G331's independently geometric uniform cone; D consists of ACTUAL infima of nonempty decreasing C-nets. Inputs must belong to D and satisfy a finite bound -M<=u<=0. Every representing term then already satisfies this bound. Arbitrary bounded functions are not declared geometric.

The arity is n-1 potentials with an nth test. Nonpure rings use the degree-n coefficient convention, retaining lower-dimensional boundary pieces with zero top-degree contribution. Curves have zero potential slots; dimension-zero reduction has empty boundary and zero measure, without negative arity. Zero/unit and permitted mixed-zero inputs are included; bottom and unbounded potential inputs are excluded. Normalization retains full conductor fibres, including the infinite-value identification stratum. Literal classical/CLD radial extension remains a separate comparison.

Actual and expanded note summaries and bodies differ and were judged separately; IDs and support arrays agree. All expanded bodies occur exactly in the complete argument. Labels, historical reading flags and candidate=false were treated as data, not correctness evidence. These conclusions remain an unverified independent-review draft.

notes.summary: The all-field primary mixed-multiplicity kernel is independently supported, without a Cartier or locality conclusion.
notes.detailedSummary: The reconstruction checks simultaneous superficial choices for both tuples, polynomial product/power linearity, integral-closure invariance, and full-boundary function/test positivity. Finite residue-field passage is algebraic only. Unit slots and nonpure top-degree coefficients are handled separately.
notes.text:
The complete reconstructed proof is whole-proof.md R2; exact primary applications are in whole-source-application-ledger.md. The current July2024 Swanson–Huneke immediate statements and proofs were freshly inspected, including 1.1.5, 6.8.1–4, 8.4.1–2, 11.1.3–5, 11.2.3–7, 17.1.6, 17.2.1–4 and 17.4.2–8. Essential integral-closure bars were confirmed on printed page140/PDF page154. Published historical foundations are disclosed, not recursively freshly reproved.

The multigraded length polynomial defines degree-n mixed coefficients. Product linearity follows by identifying the variables for I,J: terms with shared exponent one come only from original exponents (1,0) and (0,1). Power substitution gives single-slot power linearity; relabeling gives symmetry. Unit slots are separately zero because their variable is absent, without enlarging the proper-primary source hypothesis.

For J subset K with other primary slots fixed, pass algebraically to R(Z) for infinite residue field; faithful flatness and residue-field composition series preserve dimensions and lengths. Choose the SAME element in a fixed slot superficial for BOTH tuples and avoiding minimal primes. The complete superficial construction removes finitely many proper subspaces of the same I/mI; their combined complement has a point over an infinite field. Apply the same quotient to both tuples and repeat. Quotient dimensions drop by one; primary ideals remain primary, and nonreduced/non-Cohen–Macaulay quotients are allowed. In dimension one, J^N subset K^N gives the length inequality and e(J)>=e(K). Reduction likewise proves primary positivity. Unit exceptions are immediate.

If K subset integral-closure(J), put L=J+K. Homogeneous integrality makes R[Lt] finite graded over R[Jt]. Generators of degrees at most h give L^(t+h) subset J^t, while J^t subset L^t. Multiplying by the other ideal powers squeezes the corresponding lengths. Along positive integer rays, division by the parameter to power n removes the fixed shift h. The leading homogeneous polynomials agree on positive rational rays and hence identically. Thus equal integral closures give equal mixed coefficients, without coefficientwise inference from arbitrary polynomial inequalities or normalized Rees-algebra finiteness.

On ALL X_a, v(A)>=v(B) iff A lies in integral-closure(B), for primary-or-unit ideals. Forward implication uses centred rank-one DVRs on each positive-dimensional domain component and minimal-component assembly. Conversely, after quotienting by ANY semivaluation support, an ideal-integrality equation forbids a uniquely smallest leading term. Unit cases are handled separately. Minimal-support testing does not delete other supports.

For rational inputs u_i=-v(I_i)/k_i, define B_u(v(J))=e(I_1,...,I_(n-1),J)/product(k_i). Equal profiles and rational test relations become equal ideal values after powers/products; integral-closure invariance proves representation independence. A nonnegative difference v(A)-v(B) gives A subset integral-closure(B), so monotonicity and invariance prove positivity on the entire rational test lattice. Input order is u<=w implies B_u(v(J))>=B_w(v(J)); profile addition corresponds to ideal products. This establishes the stated algebraic kernel, not independent geometric model intersections.

notes.summary: Real C and actual bounded-D moment extension is supported, including weak decreasing-net continuity with a specified bounded-D limit.
notes.detailedSummary: The review reconstructs Riesz positivity, common bounds, negative-shift estimates, representation independence, scalar order and additivity. It does not assume increasing function closure, arbitrary infimum closure or nested-net flattening, and does not infer locality.
notes.text:
Full arguments are whole-proof.md R3. For rational tuples, positivity on the dense rational test lattice and rational constants q>||f|| give |B(f)|<=qB(1), hence norm boundedness. Uniform extension is real-linear by rational scalar approximation and positive by adding vanishing positive errors to approximants of nonnegative tests. Compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation supplies a finite positive Radon measure; it supplies no geometric intersection theorem.

For inputs in [-M,0], comparison with the legitimate negative constant -M gives 0<=B_u(v(J))<=M^p E_J and mass<=M^p e(a), where p=n-1 and E_J=e(a repeated p times,J). For p=0 the factor is one. These are scalar ideal-moment bounds, not order of measures.

For two tuples with slotwise uniform error at most epsilon, compare u_i-epsilon<=w_i and conversely. Expanding negative constant shifts bounds each nonempty subset S by epsilon^|S| M^(p-|S|)E_J, giving |B_u(v(J))-B_w(v(J))|<=[(M+epsilon)^p-M^p]E_J. Rational approximants to arbitrary real C inputs have a common enlarged bound; this estimate makes gauge moments Cauchy and approximation independent. Positivity, bounded mass and test density give weak convergence on every continuous test. Additivity, real nonnegative homogeneity, symmetry and scalar order pass by these approximations.

For bounded D inputs use ACTUAL decreasing C representations and their finite product directed set. Every term shares the bound [-M,0]. Gauge moments increase and remain bounded, so define their finite supremum. Difference-test values converge and again give a positive bounded functional. This is an increasing scalar limit, not increasing closure of functions.

For representation independence, fix continuous terms f_beta of one representation. The increasing open sets {g_alpha<f_beta+epsilon} from the other representation cover the compact boundary, because their infimum is the same input. A finite subcover and directedness give one common index per slot. Then g_alpha-epsilon<=f_beta; scalar order and the shift estimate bound the f-moment by the supremum of g-moments plus the displayed vanishing error. Taking suprema, epsilon down to zero and reversing roles proves equality. The same argument proves bounded-D scalar order.

Addition uses a finite product of actual representing nets, whose sum is an actual decreasing C-net to the bounded sum. Passing to bounded scalar limits proves additivity; scaling is analogous, with scalar zero giving zero. No nested-net flattening is invoked. One obtains B_u(v(J))=sup{B_g(v(J)): g_i in C and g_i>=u_i}. This is a scalar majorant formula, not a new D-membership definition.

Suppose bounded-D tuples u_lambda decrease to a SPECIFIED bounded-D tuple u, with a common finite bound. Order gives moments bounded above by the target. For any continuous C-majorants g>=u, upper semicontinuity makes {u_lambda<g+epsilon} an increasing open cover. Compactness gives a common eventual index in every slot. Thus the moments are at least B_g minus the shift error. Taking liminf, epsilon down to zero and the majorant supremum proves convergence of every gauge moment; density and bounded masses prove weak NET convergence. No arbitrary limit membership is inferred. Globally zero entries annihilate positive-arity measures; permissible mixed-zero patterns are included, while bottom/unbounded potentials remain excluded. Neither total-variation convergence nor locality follows.

notes.summary: Single-factor gauge, residue-degree normalization and smooth BFJ comparison are supported, with an explicit source-printing qualification.
notes.detailedSummary: The gauge factor is exactly v_a(b). Normalization uses actual top-dimensional centres and inseparable residue degrees, without vertical generic degrees. BFJ recovery is restricted to smooth affine closed germs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, dimension at least two. Its 4.4 proof supports nets; 4.8 alone is sequential.
notes.text:
Full reconstruction is whole-proof.md R4. The entire BFJ Setting and Section4, including immediate 4.1–4.9 proofs, were freshly inspected; printed page481/PDF page33 was visually inspected. The precise smooth domain and multiplier-dependent additivity are retained.

For primary a,b, let d(v)=v(b) on X_a and T(v)=v/d(v), transporting homogeneous inputs by u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). Pairing T_*[d nu_a] against v_b(J) cancels d and gives the same mixed coefficient. Test density identifies measures; transported uniform and actual decreasing approximations extend the identity to bounded D. Thus nu_b=T_*[d nu_a], with exactly ONE factor. For b=a^r the factor is r and potentials divide by r; substitution proves the cocycle. No nonprimary denominator is used.

For finite normalization S, reduced generic component fields are unchanged, so their module lengths are one. Mixed associativity/additivity gives e_R(...;R)=e_R(...;S). Each Artinian quotient S/AS splits into local factors; composition series contribute actual residue degree f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)] per factor. Degree-n coefficient comparison gives e_R(I_1,...,I_n)=sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q e_(S_q)(I_1S_q,...,I_nS_q). Moments, density and proved continuities yield the corresponding pushforward measure formula. Smaller-dimensional centres remain but have zero top-degree contribution. Inseparable degrees are included; normalization generic identity is not substituted for residue degree. Full conductor fibres are pushed forward, adding identified masses. This applies to pullbacks of downstairs inputs, not arbitrary upstairs operator descent or general finite-map calculus.

At a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-ZERO field, n>=2, G331 supplies full all-semivaluation class identification. Polynomial mixed coefficients equal BFJ's generic parameter quotient lengths: choose successive generic superficial parameters, use regularity/Cohen–Macaulayness, and repeatedly apply SH17.4.6. The final quotient annihilator is zero. BFJ4.7 therefore gives identical rational moments, and density identifies measures. Intersection order/additivity gives the same uniform shift estimate for real C inputs. BFJ4.4 additivity essentially uses multiplier approximation, explicitly noted in4.5; it is not transferred to singular settings.

For actual bounded decreasing C representations, Weil coefficients decrease coordinatewise to the limit. BFJ4.4 upper semicontinuity plus monotonicity gives convergence for NETS: intersection values are at least the limiting value, while their limsup is at most it. Bounded inputs and fixed Cartier tests give finite values. Dense tests identify measures on ALL semivaluations. This uses4.4's topological argument, not merely sequence-only4.8. Gauge transport handles other primary sections.

Source qualification: exact inspection of SH printed page356/PDF page370 confirms17.4.7 prints a colon-module length without the necessary quotient. For k[[x,y]] and parameters x,y, (x):y=(x) has infinite length. The correct correction is the annihilator in M/(x_1,...,x_(d-1))M, equivalently the colon module modulo that parameter submodule. The author's stated repeated17.4.6 regular-case argument uses this final quotient and remains valid. source-qualification-addendum.md records the issue; immutable sources were not edited and no author mathematical theorem required replacement. No singular Cartier comparison or open-set locality is imported.

notes.summary: The full excellent reduced-curve geometric reference theorem is supported at zero potential arity.
notes.detailedSummary: Normalization is proved finite and surjective onto every actual primary curve blowup. Independent proper Cartier degree is compared by local normalization snake cancellation, extended to all real presentations and common models. Residue/gauge weights, inseparable extensions, DVR and empty conventions are verified. This is not a positive-arity product.
notes.text:
The complete independent curve proof is whole-proof.md R5. For ANY excellent reduced local curve, finite normalization has DVR centres S_q. Every centred semivaluation of a DVR is a positive multiple of its order; maximal support would give infinite primary value. A regular conductor element has finite order on every branch, so G331 gives the entire finite discrete boundary v_q=ord_q/a_q, with singleton fibres, where a_q=ord_q(a). Define geometrically BEFORE moment comparison mu_a=sum_q f_q a_q delta_(v_q), using actual residue degrees f_q.

For EVERY actual primary blowup Y=Bl_I R, IS is invertible on the semilocal normal curve. The universal property gives h:Spec S->Y. Its graph is closed since Y is separated, and projection from Spec S times_R Y is finite by base change; hence h is finite. Its image contains every generic component point of the reduced, componentwise birational primary blowup. A finite image is closed, so h is surjective onto all Y. Locally it is the finite normal birational extension in the same total quotient fields, hence normalization. Its finite closed fibre surjects onto Y's closed fibre, which is therefore finite. This proves domination of every stated primary curve model, without arbitrary higher-dimensional cofinality.

For an effective integral exceptional Cartier divisor with regular equation g_y, define ordinary proper zero-cycle degree sum_y length(O_(Y,y)/g_y)[kappa(y):kappa(m)]. These are reduced one-dimensional local rings and finite-length quotients. At y write T=O_(Y,y), N its finite semilocal normalization and C_0=N/T, a finite-length module. Multiplication by g yields 0->C_0[g]->T/gT->N/gN->C_0/gC_0->0. Kernel and cokernel of multiplication on the same finite-length C_0 have equal length, so length_T(T/gT)=length_T(N/gN). DVR factors give sum_(q->y)[kappa(q):kappa(y)]ord_q(g). Multiplying residue degrees and summing yields deg_R(A)=sum_q f_q ord_q(h^*A), including inseparable degrees.

G331's actual Cartier order unit writes every exceptional integral divisor as a difference of effective ones. Effective degree additivity follows from the exact sequence for regular g,h: 0->T/hT->T/(gh)T->T/gT->0. Thus degree extends unambiguously to differences and all finite REAL presentations. G331 evaluation is ord_q(h^*F)/a_q; pairing the independently defined measure gives integral f_F dmu_a=deg_R(F). Under common primary-model pullback, the maps from normalization compose uniquely and Cartier orders are unchanged; the degree formula proves actual model independence.

Only afterward, normalization multiplicity additivity and the DVR formula e(J)=ord(J) give e_R(J)=sum_q f_q ord_q(J)=integral v(J)dmu_a. Hence the geometric reference agrees with zero-potential moments without circularly defining intersections. G331 descent makes every finite nonpositive branch vector continuous geometric; extended vectors have actual decreasing representations, and bounded vectors are already continuous. Mixed-zero patterns do not assert literal radial extension.

There are ZERO potentials. The sole zero-tuple has the same measure on every open set, so locality and decreasing-net continuity are true constant equalities at precisely zero arity. Changing gauge multiplies branch mass by b_q/a_q, exactly one factor. A DVR over its own residue field has maximal-ideal mass one; dimension-zero reduction has empty boundary and zero measure.

For any finite extension k subset l of degree d>1, possibly inseparable, R=k+t l[[t]] is finite over excellent A=k[[t]], via the module decomposition A plus sum_(i>=2)tA alpha_i. It is Noetherian, excellent, a one-dimensional local domain with maximal ideal tS and residue k. S=l[[t]] is finite normalization. For EVERY s in S, ts is in R, so s=(ts)/t proves Frac R=l((t)): generic degree one, residue degree d. Conductor is tS; a conductor element with nonzero k-constant would force l=k by multiplication by all l-constants. For J=t^rS, J^N=t^(rN)S and the basis 1 plus alpha_j t^i, 1<=i<rN, gives length_R(R/J^N)=1+d(rN-1) and e_R(J)=dr. The reference is d delta_ord_t. Its Cartier interpretation is on an actual model: Bl_J R=Spec S, since the t^r-chart is S and every degree-one Rees generator has square divisible by t^rT. Replacing residue degree by generic degree would incorrectly give r.

notes.summary: The nilpotent and nonpure diagnostics are supported; the two-point toy does not disprove the primary kernel.
notes.detailedSummary: Identical reduced boundary/gauge data cannot recover different unreduced generic lengths. The declared top-degree convention can annihilate nonzero lower-component inputs. The toy refutes only a bare implication from positivity and continuity to locality. Fresh checks are exhaustive only on 48 curve, eight nilpotent and 27 gauge arithmetic cases.
notes.text:
For excellent local R_1=k[[t]] and R_2=k[[t]][epsilon]/(epsilon^2), (t) is primary and semivaluations kill epsilon, so reduced boundary/gauge data coincide. Their quotients have bases t^i and t^i,epsilon t^i for 0<=i<N, giving lengths N,2N and multiplicities1,2. Thus a rule using only reduced boundary/gauge cannot recover arbitrary unreduced intersection lengths without extra generic-length information. This does not obstruct reduced P12.4.

R=k[[x,y,z]]/(xy,xz) is reduced because its defining ideal equals (x) intersection (y,z). It is the excellent local fibre product k[[y,z]] times_k k[[x]], with finite normalization their product and quotient k. Its conductor is the pair of maximal ideals, corresponding to m. All centred points have finite conductor value, so full surface and curve boundary pieces are disjoint and clopen. I_N=(y,z,x^N) is primary; its profile -v(I_N)/N equals -1/N on the surface and -1 on the curve. It converges uniformly to a C-function u equal to zero on the surface and -1 at the curve, without increasing-D closure. Degree-two normalization gives e_R(I_N,m)=1; the curve has no degree-two term, and surface monomial counting gives length(k[[y,z]]/m^t)=t(t+1)/2. The measures have mass1/N and tend weakly to zero by positivity. Thus nu_m(u)=0 despite u nonzero. This is a declared top-degree degeneracy, not deletion of a boundary component.

On discrete {x,y}, F(u)=(-u(x)-u(y))delta_x is positive, additive, nonnegative-real homogeneous and uniformly continuous; coordinate convergence also gives bounded decreasing-net continuity. Inputs (-1,-1),(-1,-2) agree on open {x}, but restricted output masses are2,3. Therefore those abstract properties alone do not imply locality. F is not shown to satisfy the actual primary kernel and is not a counterexample to its locality or to reduced P12.4.
